notes.purpose: Shows one unit's sensor readings with a short history and lets the worker see and set the ventilation fan.

elements.name: Reading tiles
elements.shows: Temperature 22.4 °C · Humidity 64 % · Ammonia 8 ppm, with "Offline · last reading 09:40" above them

states.when: The unit has a finite numeric reading for it
states.shows: A tile with the sensor name, the large value and its unit (°C, %, ppm); the first tile is selected on entry (well fill, bold label, ink bar); tapping a tile switches the trend below

states.when: Reading missing or not a finite number
states.shows: The tile is omitted, never shown as 0

states.when: None of the three has a value
states.shows: No tiles or trend; only the fan, if any

elements.logic: Sample figures per unit (Unit 7: 22.4 °C, 64 %, 8 ppm). The caption above the tiles is unitContext[N].updated, one fixed sample time for every sensor: "Offline · last reading 09:40" when offline, "Updated 09:40" when connected. The value carries no in-range or out-of-range mark because no thresholds exist yet.

elements.name: Trend group
elements.shows: Section header "Temperature" with a Today | 7 days toggle; the chart; Low 21.9 · High 22.8; Reading history ›

states.shows: 8 points; the x labels are the first and last time (00:00 and the reading time)
7 daily points; the x labels are "6d ago" and "Today"

elements.logic: Not real history: series = current value plus fixed offsets scaled by sensor (temperature ×1, humidity ×6, ammonia ×2); y range = min/max ± padding, drawn without y-axis labels because Low and High say it. Low and High are the min and max of the plotted points; only the last point carries a dot. The period control is a quiet Lens on the section header line. Reading history is the last row of the same group and opens a table of the same points.

elements.name: Connection
elements.shows: Offline · last reading 09:40 above the tiles; the fan control in its disabled state

states.when: Page default (the "Connection preview" select outside the phone)
states.shows: "Offline · last reading 09:40" above the tiles (the readings are the last available values); the fan's Auto/Manual in its disabled state (dashed rim); no Save button and no extra line
"Updated 09:40" above the tiles; fan controls enabled

elements.name: Ventilation fan card
elements.shows: Section "Ventilation fan" · Auto · unit schedule · Auto/Manual

states.shows: "Auto · unit schedule"
"Manual · N%" (initial speed 45)

states.when: The unit has no controllable device (devices lacks "fan")
states.shows: The fan section is absent; only sensors show

elements.logic: Controllable devices are independent of readings: a unit can have devices with no readings (the unit card then says "N devices") or readings with no device.
elements.rule: Save setting appears only in Manual or with a pending change, and is disabled until the draft differs from the saved setting; offline it is absent. Nothing is sent to equipment (the PREVIEW badge says so); the setting lives in memory only.

copy: (raw) every string is literal in home-astra-prototype.js; the registry has no environment ids
edge: A unit with neither readings nor devices has no environment entrance on its Home screen.
issues: The time in the caption above the tiles is a fixed 09:40 on all sensors while the status bar reads 9:41.
Only a ventilation fan exists; the concept names "devices" in general.
unclear: alert thresholds, who is told when a reading is out of range, and where real data comes from; none are in the code.

notes.purpose: Lets the worker set a fixed fan speed instead of the unit schedule.

elements.name: Fan speed and Save

states.when: Manual pressed, speed moved, not applied
states.shows: Slider 0-100 in steps of 5 with a live value; Save setting enabled once the draft differs from the saved setting
Status "Manual · 70%" and the toast "Fan setting saved"
The slider goes away; a draft equal to the saved state keeps Save disabled

elements.rule: The draft is not applied until Save; everything is disabled offline. The PREVIEW badge says no command is sent to equipment.

issues: No confirmation or safety limit for speed 0; unclear whether 0% is allowed on a real fan.

screens.name: Maintenance · open issue
screens.zh: 维修 · 有未解决问题

notes.purpose: Lists the unit's equipment issues and lets the worker report one.

elements.name: Issue card
elements.shows: Drinking station · Open · Pen C2 · Leaking valve at the east end. · G. Hansen · 06:40

states.shows: Equipment name, "Open", the note, then one line: location · reporter · time
Dimmed with "Resolved"; stays in the list
Reporter reads "G. Hansen · just now", at the top of the list

elements.logic: Location and note are free text typed by the reporter.
elements.at: Leaking valve at the east end.

elements.name: Open issues
elements.shows: Section "Issues": one row per issue, and "Report issue" as the last row of the same group; no count line
elements.logic: The list is the count; the count line was cut. The unit screen's Maintenance chip carries the number of records not resolved. Unit 7 starts with one open issue; the `attention` param hides it (clear, health, feed) or adds a default one in other units (maintenance, busy).
elements.rule: Only reachable once a unit is chosen: the Toolbox row exists only in a unit scope. Issues are unit-scoped.

edge: Resolved issues stay listed, so the list is not empty after the only issue is resolved.
issues: The path here is Toolbox, two taps from the unit; the unit screen's Maintenance chip does not link here.
No photo, priority, assignee, or history of who resolved it.

notes.purpose: The empty state when the unit has no issue.

states.when: The unit has no records at all (Unit 8)
states.shows: Section "Issues" with the row "No open issues" and the Report issue row
Not this state: the resolved cards stay listed

notes.purpose: Captures a new equipment issue in three fields.

elements.name: Form and Save
elements.shows: Equipment · Location in Unit 7 · What needs attention? · Save sample issue
elements.logic: Equipment (max 80) and Location (max 80, label names the unit) are free text; Note is a textarea (max 500). Save adds an open record at the top with reporter "G. Hansen · just now", closes the drawer and toasts "Issue saved in this preview".
elements.rule: All three fields are required; whitespace-only values are ignored.

issues: Equipment and location are free text; no list of the unit's devices or pens is offered.

notes.purpose: Shows one issue and lets the worker mark it resolved.

elements.name: Mark resolved
elements.logic: Sets resolved on the record, closes the drawer and toasts "Issue resolved in this preview"; the open count drops.
elements.rule: No note is asked and no resolver or time is recorded.

issues: Resolving needs no note and records no resolver or time.

elements.name: Resolved line
elements.shows: Pen C2 · Resolved · Resolved in this preview.

states.shows: The Mark resolved button is replaced by a static line; no action is offered

elements.rule: A resolved issue cannot be reopened.

notes.purpose: The same sensor page switched from today to the last seven days.

elements.name: Chart and low/high
elements.shows: Seven daily points (6d ago to Today) with low and high; Reading history is the last row of the trend group
elements.logic: The week series is sample data derived from the current reading; the Today series has eight points up to the reading time. Low and High are the minimum and maximum of the plotted points; the Reading history row opens a table of the same points.

issues: The chart switch does not change the caption time (still 09:40).

notes.purpose: The sensor page with another sensor selected.

elements.name: Sensor switch
elements.shows: Segment of the sensors the unit has: Temperature, Humidity, Ammonia

states.shows: That sensor is omitted from the switch, never shown as 0

states.when: Only one sensor has a reading
states.shows: The switch lists only it; the page opens on it

elements.logic: Unit and chart scale differ per sensor (°C, %, ppm NH₃); the plotted range is padded by 0.5 for temperature and 1 for the others.
